'''Barbara Schaffner''' (born 28 July 1968) is a Swiss politician, energy expert, and [[physicist]]. She is a member of the [[National Council (Switzerland)|National Council]] for the [[Green Liberal Party of Switzerland|Green Liberal Party]] for the [[canton of Zurich]] and mayor of [[Otelfingen]].

== Biography ==
Barbara Schaffner grew up in {{Interlanguage link|Anglikon|de}} in the canton of [[Aargau]]. In 1988 she lived as an exchange student on a farm in [[Wyoming]], [[United States|USA]]. After studying [[physics]] and receiving a doctorate in [[medical physics]]<ref>{{Cite thesis |last1=Schaffner |first1=Barbara |title=Range precision of therapeutic proton beams |date=1997 |publisher=ETH Zürich |doi=10.3929/ethz-a-001891967 |hdl=20.500.11850/143426}}</ref> at [[ETH Zurich|ETH Zürich]] and the P[[Paul Scherrer Institute]], she completed a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoc]] at the [[National Institute of Radiological Sciences]] in [[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba]], [[Japan]]. From 2000 to 2008 she worked at [[Varian Medical Systems]] as a specialist in [[proton therapy]] and researched [[algorithm]]s in [[radiotherapy]]<ref name="CV" /> At ETH, Schaffner furthered her education, obtaining a Master of Energy Science and Technology, worked as a project manager for [[Photovoltaics|solar power plants]] and, as an energy expert, is the managing director of her company eneba GmbH.  As managing director and board member, she heads the non-partisan networking group ''Zurich Renewable: Association for Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energies. Furthermore, as a member of the board of the Mühle Otelfingen Foundation'', she is committed to preserving the historic building and using it for cultural events.<ref>{{Webarchive|url=http://furu.zehnder.ch/eweb/furu/2019/02/22/FU/7/2862/|wayback=20190818103316|text=In der Mühle wird frisch gemahlen}}, Malini Gloor in Furttaler Nachrichten 22 January 2019, retrieved 13 August 2019.</ref> She has two children with her long-term partner, Paul Eggimann.

== Political career ==
Schaffner was elected to the [[Cantonal Council of Zurich]] for the [[Dielsdorf District|Dielsdorf district]] in 2011. She was a member of the ''Committee for Transport, Energy and the Environment''.<ref>{{Webarchive|url=https://www.kantonsrat.zh.ch/mitglieder/mitglieder.aspx|wayback=20191227080835|text=Homepage Kantonsrat Zürich}}, retrieved 13 August 2019.</ref> From 2011 to 2013, she was also a member of the ''Committee for Planning and Construction''. In the Cantonal Council, she campaigned primarily for renewable energies  and public transport. She also attracted attention with a successful<ref>[https://kantonsrat-zh.talus.ch/de/politik/cdws/dok_geschaeft.php?did=5cc5b58a6c484699bcfe14fc5da13081-332&v=1&r=PDF&filename=Abstimmungsresultat&typ=pdf Abstimmungsprotokoll Zürcher Rathaus 24 February 2014]{{Dead link|url=https://kantonsrat-zh.talus.ch/de/politik/cdws/dok_geschaeft.php?did=5cc5b58a6c484699bcfe14fc5da13081-332&v=1&r=PDF&filename=Abstimmungsresultat&typ=pdf|date=October 2022}}, Homepage des Kantonsrats, retrieved 17 August 2019.</ref> initiative<ref>[https://kantonsrat-zh.talus.ch/de/politik/cdws/dok_geschaeft.php?did=c7ba22b3ef034c919fd3d6493dcd5bee-332&v=1&r=PDF&filename=Dringliches_Postulat_359-2013_Rettung_der_einheimischen_Krebsarten&typ=pdf Dringliches Postulat ''Rettung einheimischer Krebsarten'']{{Dead link|url=https://kantonsrat-zh.talus.ch/de/politik/cdws/dok_geschaeft.php?did=c7ba22b3ef034c919fd3d6493dcd5bee-332&v=1&r=PDF&filename=Dringliches_Postulat_359-2013_Rettung_der_einheimischen_Krebsarten&typ=pdf|date=October 2022}}, 9 December 2013, Homepage des Kantonsrats, retrieved 17 August 2019.</ref> against the disappearance of native [[crayfish]] species.

In July 2018, the voters of Otelfingen elected Schaffner as mayor. In 2019, she was one of the driving forces with the committee ''"No to the harmful water law"'' that defeated the new water law in the canton of Zurich in a referendum, arguing primarily with environmental and flood protection as well as the additional bureaucratic burden for municipalities. In the [[Green Liberal Party of Switzerland|GLP]], she heads the national energy working group and is president of the GLP Unteres Furttal. In the [[2019 Swiss federal election|parliamentary elections on 20 October 2019]], Schaffner was elected to the National Council for the Green Liberals. She therefore resigned from the Cantonal Council in November 2019. In the National Council, she is (as of August 2024) in the {{Interlanguage link|Committees for Transport and Telecommunications of the Federal Council|de|Kommissionen für Verkehr und Fernmeldewesen der Eidgenössischen Räte}}, in the Delegation for Relations with the Parliament of the Principality of Liechtenstein and deputy in the Parliamentary IT Group (PIT).
